statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $Y \subset X$ be an irreducible closed subset.
Let $U \subset X$ be an open subset such that $Y \cap U$ is nonempty.
Then
$$
\text{codim}(Y, X) = \text{codim}(Y \cap U, U)
$$

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-codimension-at-generic-point}
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $Y \subset X$ be an irreducible closed subset.
Let $U \subset X$ be an open subset such that $Y \cap U$ is nonempty.
Then
$$
\text{codim}(Y, X) = \text{codim}(Y \cap U, U)
$$

Catenarity is local on open covers, and the catenary condition passes to locally closed subspaces. Both directions of the open-cover characterization and the additional hereditary conclusion remain.
statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is catenary,
\item $X$ has an open covering by catenary spaces.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, in this case any locally closed subspace of $X$ is catenary.

Catenarity is characterized by finite codimensions for nested irreducible closed subsets and additivity of codimensions along triples. The finiteness and additivity conditions are jointly required and the iff is retained.
statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is catenary, and
\item for every pair of irreducible closed subsets $Y \subset Y'$ we have
$\text{codim}(Y, Y') < \infty$ and for every triple
$Y \subset Y' \subset Y''$ of irreducible closed subsets we have
$$
\text{codim}(Y, Y'') = \text{codim}(Y, Y') + \text{codim}(Y', Y'').
$$
\end{enumerate}
